findings.summary: 'latency' counts as a speed cue on its own, so feature requests about measuring latency would be refused
findings.evidence: The plan rules out bare delay, timing and slow because they are common in requests that are not about speed, but keeps 'latency' as a stand-alone cue. 'Show p95 latency in athena status' asks for a new feature, yet it would need a stage timeline. No accept case covers this. Fix: Treat 'latency' like the weak words (it counts only after a cut verb within five words or after 'too'), or add an accept case like 'Show p95 latency in athena status' and make it pass.

findings.summary: The plan says text written by others is never scanned, but the root-cause Cause line and title are scanned
findings.evidence: hestia.rs:463-464 says the cause text comes from introspections a person or a model wrote. The plan keeps scanning the 'Cause:' line (hestia.rs:473) and the title, which is built from the cause text (hestia.rs:496). That is right for the class, but it contradicts the rule as stated. Fix: In Decision 2, D163 and the doc comment, say that the Cause line and title are scanned on purpose because the cause is the request's subject, and that only the prevention lines, the spec statement and the approved proposal's Source and Evidence are skipped.

findings.summary: No test for durations written with no space ('40s', '9min')
findings.evidence: request_words (reading.rs:3503-3524) keeps runs of letters and digits together, so '40s' and '9min' are single words, while '40 s' is two. The demonstrations only use the spaced form ('compile 9 min, check 40 s'). Fix: Add a unit test where a Timeline stage duration has no space (e.g. 'compile 9min, check 40s') and is accepted, and handle both forms in the 'under N minutes' cue.

summary: Round 5 plan adds one step, check_speed_timeline, to refusing_check after check_outcome_state (reading.rs:3248), so the position checked by the order test at reading.rs:7735-7743 does not move. The supporting claims hold in the snapshot. spec_request sets High only when gap.speed holds (hestia.rs:726-730), and Priority::from_text reads the Priority line (plan.rs:97). approve_request copies cited records only after '## Source' (work_decisions.rs:285-305). SPEC_LINE is a private const at hestia.rs:520, and THROUGHPUT_MARKER and SLOWDOWN_MARKER are pub consts at :1304 and :1314. The fake reader's assumption (fake.rs:283) and the 'Speed up planning' drain request (drain.rs:7012) exist, and 'not exist' is in ABSENCE_PHRASES (reading.rs:3030). replay, replay_declaration, names_crates_path and design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended all exist. The corpus fixture lists crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, so the accept cases also pass check_reading_references. Each demonstration names a real seam, and each would fail without the step or the rule it covers. The dependents list matches the readers I found. Detecting speed requests by word cues is a heuristic, but the accepted reading chose it, and each rule is tied to a corpus case. I considered the reading's urgent_reason field as an alternative signal; it also covers failed attempts and redo work, so it is too broad to replace the cues. Remaining issues: two minor and one nit. 'latency' counts on its own and will refuse feature requests about latency. Decision 2 says no text written by others is scanned, but the Cause line and title of root-cause requests are scanned. Durations written with no space need a test. Athena's four scope findings are minor and justified: each file is needed, sits under Files: crates/, and is named in the changelog and D163.
